scenes.heading: Equivalent fractions and simplifying
scenes.say: Is two eighths of a pizza the same as one quarter? Yes it is! Today you'll learn how fractions can look different but be exactly the same size, and how to write them in their simplest form.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: 1 slice of a pizza cut in 4 = 2 slices of the same pizza cut in 8
scenes.science: 1/4 = 2/8: same amount, more but smaller pieces
scenes.breaks: Real slices are never exactly equal. In maths every piece must be the same size.
scenes.say: Picture a pizza cut into four slices. Take one: that's one quarter. Now cut the same pizza into eight slices. You need two slices to get the same amount. One quarter equals two eighths. More pieces, smaller pieces, same pizza.
scenes.caption: Picture a pizza cut into 4 slices. Take 1: that's 1/4. Cut the same pizza into 8 slices and you need 2 to get the same amount. 1/4 = 2/8. More pieces, smaller pieces, same pizza.

scenes.heading: Key ideas
points: Numerator (top) = how many parts you have
Multiply top AND bottom by the same number
Divide top and bottom by a common factor to simplify
scenes.say: The bottom number, the denominator, tells you how many equal parts. The top number, the numerator, tells you how many you have. To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. To simplify, divide them both by the same number.

scenes.heading: Why it works
scenes.say: Why does this work? Multiplying top and bottom by four is the same as multiplying by four quarters, which is just one. Multiplying by one never changes a number. So two thirds equals eight twelfths.
scenes.caption: Multiplying top and bottom by 4 is the same as multiplying by 4/4, which is just 1. Multiplying by 1 never changes a number. So 2/3 = 8/12.

scenes.heading: Worked example
scenes.question: Write 2/5 with a denominator of 15.
scenes.say: Write two fifths with a denominator of fifteen. Fifteen divided by five is three, so multiply the top by three as well. Two times three is six. Two fifths equals six fifteenths.
scenes.caption: Write 2/5 with a denominator of 15. 15 ÷ 5 = 3, so multiply the top by 3 too. 2 × 3 = 6. 2/5 = 6/15.

scenes.heading: Simplifying
scenes.question: Simplify 36/48.
lines: Or in one go: HCF is 12, so 3/4
scenes.say: Simplify thirty-six forty-eighths. If you can't see the biggest common factor, go in small steps. Halve both: eighteen twenty-fourths. Halve again: nine twelfths. Divide both by three: three quarters. Or divide by the highest common factor, twelve, in one step.
scenes.caption: Simplify 36/48. Go in small steps. Halve both: 18/24. Halve again: 9/12. Divide both by 3: 3/4. Or divide by the HCF, 12, in one step.

scenes.heading: Do this, not that
scenes.say: Watch out for the most common mistake: adding the same number to the top and bottom. Two thirds is not three quarters! Only multiply or divide, and always do the same to both numbers.
scenes.caption: Watch out for the most common mistake: adding the same number to the top and bottom. 2/3 is not 3/4! Only multiply or divide, and always do the same to both numbers.

points: × or ÷ top and bottom by the same number
scenes.closing: What you do to the top, do to the bottom!
scenes.say: Quick recap. Equivalent fractions are the same amount. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. A fraction is in simplest form when only one divides into both. Compare fractions using a common denominator. Now try the practice questions!
